issue.title: [Bug] list_directory leaks all hidden files/dotfiles by default due to !dirPath.startsWith('.')
issue.body:
## Description

When calling the `list_directory` tool without specifying a `path` parameter, `dirPath` defaults to `'.'`. Inside `walkDirectory()`, dotfiles are meant to be skipped unless `showHiddenFiles` is `true`. However, the skip condition contains `!dirPath.startsWith('.')`. Because `'.'.startsWith('.')` is `true`, `!dirPath.startsWith('.')` evaluates to `false`, which bypasses the filter and leaks all hidden files and directories (`.env`, `.git`, `.vscode`, `.DS_Store`, etc.) into the tool output.

## Environment

- **OS**: Linux / macOS / Windows
- **Node version**: v22.20.0
- **Nanocoder version**: 1.30.0
- **Provider**: Any
- **Model**: Any

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have hidden files in the project root directory (e.g. `.env`, `.config`, `.nanocoder-history`).
2. Run `list_directory` with default arguments: `{}` or `{ path: '.' }` or `{ path: './src' }`.
3. Check the returned directory listing.

## Expected Behavior

With `showHiddenFiles: false` (the default), hidden files and directories should be excluded from directory listings.

## Actual Behavior

Every dotfile and hidden directory in the directory is printed in the listing. Even in `source/tools/list-directory.spec.tsx`, line 556 had to work around this bug:
```typescript
// List a subdirectory explicitly (not the current dir) to hide dotfiles
```

## Logs/Screenshots

In `source/tools/list-directory.tsx`:
```typescript
const dirPath = args.path || '.';
...
// Skip hidden files unless showHiddenFiles is true
if (
    !showHiddenFiles &&
    item.name.startsWith('.') &&
    !dirPath.startsWith('.')
) {
    continue;
}
```

## Additional Context

- [x] I have searched existing issues to ensure this is not a duplicate
- [x] I can reproduce this issue consistently
- [x] This issue occurs with the latest version of nanocoder

## Implementation Notes (optional)

- N/A

steps:
Set up a small fixture in the workspace by running this exact shell command:
mkdir -p .git
n=zzhiddenmarker
printf 'MARKER=hidden-ok\n' > ".$n"
mkdir -p ".$n-dir"
printf 'x\n' > ".$n-dir/entry.txt"
printf 'ref: refs/heads/main\n' > .git/HEAD

When it finishes, just reply 'fixture ready' — don't describe the files.
Run the list_directory tool with default arguments (`{}`) on the current directory and show me the raw output.
expected: With `showHiddenFiles: false` (the default), a `list_directory` call whose path defaults to '.' must exclude every entry whose name starts with '.', so the returned listing must not contain the fixture dotfile/dotdir (`.zzhiddenmarker`, `.zzhiddenmarker-dir`) — per the issue's Expected Behavior and the tool's own 'skip hidden files unless showHiddenFiles is true' contract.
defect: `walkDirectory()`'s skip condition `!showHiddenFiles && item.name.startsWith('.') && !dirPath.startsWith('.')` is bypassed for the default path '.' (because '.'.startsWith('.') is true), so list_directory dumps all hidden files and directories (.env, .git, .zzhiddenmarker, …) into the output; fixed in 1.31.0 by PR #1253.

fault location.explanation: Contributing source location. See Root cause and the evidence review for observed behavior and limitations.

Root cause: The hidden-file skip condition additionally requires !dirPath.startsWith("."). For the default directory ".", that condition is false, disabling the hidden-entry filter. The retained default listing exposes .zzhiddenmarker and .zzhiddenmarker-dir. The absence of .git from that output does not negate the other hidden-entry leak.
